description: torch's `channels_last` for 4-D tensors: NCHW logical, NHWC in storage. The arrangement inductor's conv lowering wants and re-derives on every forward call when the weights do not already have it.
name: torch.channels_last-2d
provenance: MEASURED, not assumed (tcg#82, banked in research/layout-morphisms/0-DESIGN.md §9): SDXL's UNet carries 635 MiB of conv weights, 13.0% of its 4.78 GiB constant set, and inductor re-transposes them to NHWC every forward — >=1.27 GiB of DRAM traffic per step, ~36 GiB per 28-step image. Delivering the weights already in this arrangement is what makes that traffic zero.

READ FROM TORCH SOURCE, not inferred: `_inductor/ir.py`'s `require_strides` emits NO copy when the strides already match. That is the whole mechanism this record exists to trigger — the 51 per-call permute kernels are never generated, rather than generated and made cheap.
The permutation is torch's own `memory_format=torch.channels_last` and is not a choice made here: storage order (N, H, W, C) over logical axes (N, C, H, W) is axes [0, 2, 3, 1].
